The core insight lies in leveraging geometric constraints to reduce combinatorial complexity. By selecting a minimal subset (Nmin=3) of positional and sensing units, one can compute the rigid-body transformation (R, r) that aligns them. This transformation then constrains all other pairs under the same linked-segment model. The brute-force approach scales factorially with N, making it impractical for large N. Thus, the system trades exhaustive search for structured inference. The presence of multiple minima does not degrade performance, but reducing their likelihood improves robustness. The key duality is between full enumeration and constraint-driven reduction—whereby the former is computationally prohibitive while the latter enables scalable solutions through geometric reasoning.
